name: F-5 Tiger II
summary: Small, light twin-jet fighter used by Navy and Marine Corps adversary squadrons to simulate enemy fighters, often in exotic camouflage.

wings: Small thin trapezoidal wing, mounted low on the fuselage
Small leading-edge root extensions blending into the intakes
Wingtip missile rails, usually with training missiles
engines: Two small engines with exhausts close together at the tail
Small side intakes just behind the cockpit
fuselage: Single-seat bubble canopy (F model has two seats)
Waisted (area-ruled) fuselage, often in blue-grey or desert aggressor camouflage

tellTales: Tiny fighter with a needle nose and missiles on the wingtips
Two small exhausts side by side under a single fin
Small wing-root extensions blending into side intakes

confusedWith.howToTell: The F-5 has wing-root extensions, wingtip missile rails and usually a single seat in camouflage; the T-38 is a slim two-seat trainer with no LERX or wingtip rails.
The F-5 has small side intakes and two exhausts; the F-16 has a big chin intake under the nose and one large exhaust.

usCount.source: NAVAIR adversary program / Seapower Magazine (44 F-5N/F plus ex-Swiss additions)
